$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccscx)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-7arccscx) \\  & =-7\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\right) \\  & =\frac{7}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line to the curve $y=f(x)$ at $x=\sqrt{5}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\sqrt{5}) & =\frac{7}{|\sqrt{5}|\sqrt{{\sqrt{5}}^{2}-1}} \\  & =\frac{7}{\sqrt{5}\sqrt{5-1}} \\  & =\frac{7}{2\sqrt{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$" "The formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arccsc} $ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccsc} x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-7\operatorname{arccsc} x) \\  & =-7\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\right) \\  & =\frac{7}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line to the curve $y=f(x)$ at $x=\sqrt{5}$ is

$$"] [:db/cas 17592186247133 :question/problem "Calculate ${f}^{′}(x)$ if $f(x)=2\sqrt{x}+5arccscx.$" "Calculate ${f}^{′}(x)$ if $f(x)=2\sqrt{x}+5\operatorname{arccsc} x.$"] [:db/cas 17592186247133 :question/worked-solution "The formula for the derivative of $arccsc$ is
